elements.evidence: Rendered § 12.4 now reads "Customer may solicit, hire, or employ Vendor employees without restriction." The former bar ("shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward") is gone, and no other cited provision imposes a solicitation restraint on Customer; § 12.3 affirmatively confirms Customer gave "no ... no-hire commitment."

No non-solicitation obligation survives on either side after the edit, so there is no mutual covenant in operative text; the mutual 12-month construct appears only in the margin comment as an offer, which is not operative language.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: There is no surviving restriction and no scope language limiting any covenant to personnel directly involved in the Services; the drafter chose the preferred path instead.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: No duration language exists in the rendered § 12.4 (deterministic check: "number not found"), because the covenant was deleted rather than time-limited; nothing anchors 12 months to the end of involvement.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no restriction remains from which to carve out general advertisements, and § 12.4 permits solicitation and hiring "without restriction," while § 12.3 preserves hiring of "any person who responds to general recruitment." The failed carve-out regex is mechanically correct but immaterial on this path.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no covenant in force, unsolicited approaches are unrestricted by operation of the amended § 12.4.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The prior no-hire ("solicit, hire, or employ ... regardless of how the employee applies") is deleted; § 12.4 now expressly permits Customer to "hire, or employ Vendor employees without restriction."

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single preferred element is satisfied by operative text, not merely promised in the comment — § 12.4 is converted from a term-plus-24-month solicit/hire/employ bar into an express permission, leaving no non-solicitation restraint on Customer anywhere in the cited text.

Fallback level is incomplete (mutuality, involvement-limited scope and the 12-month duration are absent), but that is irrelevant to position-completeness because the preferred checklist is fully met; the mutual 12-month alternative is correctly held in reserve in the comment rather than drafted into the clause.

Minimality holds: the edit touches only § 12.4, adds no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or extra obligation, and does not disturb § 12.3. The affirmative permission sentence overlaps slightly with § 12.3's no-no-hire acknowledgment, but it is a concise, non-duplicative way to render the deletion without leaving an empty numbered section.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is orphaned and no cross-reference dangles; the change in fact removes the retained-sentence contradiction with § 12.3 ("Customer has made no ... no-hire commitment"), and unrelated allocation, timing and commercial mechanics are untouched.

Deterministic duration and carve-out failures are substantively inapplicable on the preferred path — there is no surviving covenant to date-limit or carve out from — so they do not defeat completeness; no repair is required in operative language.
